title: Adaptive Content Tuning of Social Network Digital Health Interventions Using Control Systems Engineering for Precision Public Health: Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: A cluster-randomized California trial compared Facebook organ-donation education with and without adaptive PID content tuning across four demographic clusters over three months. Adaptive tuning increased clicks per 1,000 impressions overall (β=0.2187, P<.001), with the effect varying by cluster; clicks were a surrogate for awareness, not measured donation behavior.
ai_technology: Adaptive Content Tuning (ACT) using a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller and demographic clustering

evidence.tested: A cluster-randomized California trial compared Facebook organ-donation education with and without adaptive PID content tuning across four demographic clusters over three months. Adaptive tuning increased clicks per 1,000 impressions overall (β=0.2187, P<.001), with the effect varying by cluster; clicks were a surrogate for awareness, not measured donation behavior.
evidence.unknown: Clicks were a surrogate for awareness; actual organ donation or sustained behavior change was not measured.
evidence.ai_role: The ACT PID controller adjusted social-network educational content using engagement feedback across demographic clusters; the cluster-randomized trial reported increased engagement.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
